description: Which signature format each repository's commits take, and the commit that ends the old signing there (agent-fabric ADR-057 §5 rules 1, 3, 5); and the keys the forge signs its own commits with (rule 8). The shape is identities/schemas/signing.schema.json. A repository is named owner/name as one of its projects/registry.json remotes names it; listing it is what makes bootstrap write its working copies' signing settings (gpg.format, gpg.program and gpg.ssh.program = fabric-sign, user.signingkey, commit.gpgsign). since is the full sha on the repository's default branch from which the checker (tools/fabric/guards/ban_unsigned_commits.py) applies rule 5 to every commit not reachable from it; null: not cut over yet, and nothing is refused under rule 5. An entry's missing key is the default's. forge_keys names, by its full fingerprint, each key GitHub signs the commits it makes with, its public key committed as policies/forge-keys/<fingerprint>.asc: after since, a commit signed by one passes rule 5 only as a clean merge of its two parents or a Dependabot commit, not a merge, whose diff is not empty and lies only under .github/workflows/, and a key GitHub rotates to is refused until it is listed here. Rollout (the owner, 2026-10-13): no repository is listed until a fleet readiness check shows every account can give its key and sign a test commit; then agent-fabric first, then the rest one at a time.
